Hey Brew Shop Fam!
Here's an update of what's happening this week - from new beer drops, wine reviews, our current tap list, to upcoming tastings, and more.

We’re here to help you prep for Thanksgiving with one last tasting this week! Come hang with us from 4-6 pm on Tuesday for Wine Club Tasting with Sandy from Robins Cellars (Not a member? No worries, come see what it’s all about!)

Scroll down to see our full lineup of tastings for December.

Please note: we’ll be closed on Thursday and Friday this week. Stock up early and then we’ll see you on the other side!

We're excited to bring back The Brew Shop 12 Wines of Christmas (step aside drummers drumming!). Inside our festive box, you'll find 12 wines to sip through December. Available in limited quantities and by pre-order only, make sure you grab your box before they sell out!

Our 12 Wines of Christmas will be hand-selected by your favorite winos (Beth, Julie & Aidan) and filled with never-before-seen-in-the-shop wines perfect to pair with your holidays. What's inside is a surprise, but expect the following -- each box will contain TWO sparklers, THREE whites, SIX reds and ONE wild card. Our holiday elves will wrap each box to keep the surprises coming!

12 Wines of Christmas boxes will be available for pick-up beginning Friday, December 4th.

Starr Hill Holiday Road

Good food, great wine, and something for everyone at the table.

Thanksgiving is one of the best holidays for wine. Between the turkey, stuffing, cranberry sauce, and about a dozen different side dishes, there’s a lot going on at the dinner table. And every family tradition is different, you might be a Thanksgiving Prime Rib person! (And if you are, rude? send me an e-vite next year). Luckily, there’s no single right wine for Thanksgiving, and half the fun is finding something that works with a little bit of everything.

First things first: bubbles! Whether you’re greeting guests or sneaking hor d'oeuvres before dinner (or as my New Yorker grandma would call them, "hoos doovers"), sparkling wine is always a good place to start. The Laurent Perrachon Cremant de Bourgogne brings crisp citrus, delicate bubbles, and a touch of toasty richness for those who love Champagne vibes. For something a little more playful, Bottex Bugey Cru Cerdon is a lightly sweet, lower-alcohol sparkling rosé bursting with juicy red berries. Beth commented something along the lines of "SO GOOD!" and "SUGARPLUM FAIRIES!".....or maybe it was "sugared cranberry" and I'm getting ahead of myself for the next holiday.....If you’re looking for something fun but a little less bubbly, the Coletti Arristo Bomba Frizzante brings a little Italian sparkle to the festivities, while still being very food friendly.

When it comes to whites, acidity is your best friend. All those buttery, savory Thanksgiving dishes practically beg for something bright and refreshing. Depending on what level of acidity is your jam, we've got options for you. The Weingut Manfred Breit Riesling Trocken is lightly sweet, refreshingly acidic, and wonderfully versatile. AND comes in a liter bottle, so that's a bonus.This is a great table wine, I bring it home for the holidays every year. If you're in the mood for something a bit more zippy, Domaine du Salvard Cheverny Blanc combines freshness and texture, for another super versatile pick. You want something even MORE crispy? Say less. Francis Blanchet Pouilly-Fume Kriotine is a beautifully crispy french Sauvy B, that has a wonderful amount of minerality and a touch of sea salt. If you prefer something richer, Truchard Carneros Chardonnay brings ripe orchard fruit and a touch of creamy richness that’s right at home with mashed potatoes and gravy, or a creamy brie from your hoos doovers spread.

Now, let’s talk reds. There’s a reason Pinot Noir and Beaujolais are Thanksgiving classics: they’re fruity, fresh, and won’t bulldoze your turkey! Les Cardinaux Côte de Brouilly brings juicy red berries and a little earthy character, while Anne Amie Pinot Noir (don't get me started on how cute the bottle is) offers silky texture, bright cherry fruit, and just enough savory complexity. Both are fantastic with turkey, stuffing, and even that tricky cranberry sauce. But what about a chillable red? Even though those last two I mentioned could totally handle a light chill, let me steer you in the direction of Les Lunes Cosmic Blend. This is a crunchy, complex red blend that’s light but plush, and leans a little more blue fruit than red fruit. As Dr. Suess would say, One fruit two fruit, red fruit blue fruit. Also, not a red, but don’t count out rosé just because summer’s over! Eric Cottat Sancerre Rosé is delicate, refreshing, and a lovely match for turkey and herb-heavy sides.

But what if you like your reds a little bigger? A little bolder? Don’t worry, we haven’t forgotten about you. Let's talk French first. For some more earthy, savory pairings, a French red is your best friend. Château Trébiac Bordeaux Rouge offers dark fruit and spice, your classic Bordeaux energy. If you're looking for a dress-to-impress kind of bottle, Bonpas Châteauneuf-du-Pape brings rich berries and warming herbal notes that practically beg to be next to a plate of sausage stuffing (shout out to last week’s newsletter if you want to hear more about this bottle). For the devoted Cabernet drinkers, Growers Guild Cabernet Sauvignon is a Washington State, jammy, delightful, crowd-friendly option. For our Napa die-hards, Purlieu “Le Pich” Napa Cabernet Sauvignon brings the bold, velvety richness you’d want for a special holiday bottle. These bigger reds especially shine if there’s beef, mushrooms, or other hearty dishes on the menu (I'm looking at you, Prime Rib people. Seriously where's my invite?).

At the end of the day, the best Thanksgiving wine is the one you actually want to drink, and for me, one I'm happy to share. Grab a few different bottles, pass them around the table, and don’t worry too much about the rules. After all, Thanksgiving is about sharing good things with good people. Cheers!

This year’s Thanksgiving Wine Guide is brought to you by Aidan

Thanks for your business! See you soon, Beth, Julie & Aidan and the entire Brew Crew
